tasks.spec:
You are making the narrator's prompt PLACE-SCOPED in freytag-forge (Python 3.12): the engine already knows where the protagonist is (the world tree) and must feed the narrator what is visible from there, instead of the whole scene's house-centric text. Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. YOU MAY EDIT: storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/knowledge.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py (only what is needed), data/stories/continuity-initiative/world.yaml (ONLY one new `description` on the location outside_house), docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (one short paragraph for the new field, no other edits), tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py (NEW), tests/fixtures/place_feed/ (NEW golden prompts), and existing tests only where a pin truly changes (list each). Never edit bench/frozen/, tests/fixtures/continuity_initiative_pre_3c_adoption/, docs/testing-runbook.md; do not reformat unrelated text. Shared runtime has NO story names (no Kristin, truck, drawer, Michelle, 1A, outside_house).

MEASURED PROBLEM (live, 11 of 11 'look around' turns while Kristin was outside or seated in her truck). The narrator described the house interior and moved her into it. The recorded prompt (user text) contained: SCENE with only house content (the scene situation 'the back door has been forced... a drawer on Michelle's workstation has Kristin's initials', two committed statements 'Kristin opens the drawer and is pointed toward the thin gap...'); a THINGS/PLAYER list of about 15 house objects (drawer, pens, stapler, spare batteries, phone, workstation, chair, back door); and ONE line about the protagonist, 'Kristin. Place: driver's seat.' So the narrator had nothing but the house to describe.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR (all generic, derived from the world tree via the existing worldkeeper API: world.area, world.together, world.parent, world.chain, world.holder).
1. Optional `description: str | None` on package Locations (models.py Location; loader validates non-blank when present; document it). Add to world.yaml for outside_house exactly: Michelle's house stands behind a low gate. Kristin's truck is parked at the curb, and sirens carry from the next street.
2. Scene frame scoping (storygame/runtime/knowledge.py around line 263, where scene_frame=frame.situation is set): the scene `situation` is shown only while the protagonist is `together` with the scene's location (scene.metadata.location_id). Otherwise it is replaced by the `description` of the deepest area on the protagonist's chain that has one (empty string if none). The scene `pressure` line is unchanged.
3. Committed statements: a committed knowledge item that declares `reach_entity_ids` (already in the model) is projected into the narrator's committed knowledge only while the protagonist is together with every listed entity. Items without it are unchanged. (This hides the drawer-pointer statements while she is outside.)
4. THINGS and PLAYER lists for the NARRATION prompt (storygame/runtime/item_facts.py `_thing_names`, `_things_block`, `_player_lines`): list only the protagonist, things the protagonist holds, and things `together` with the protagonist. ALSO always keep any thing the player's own command names (the existing referred-lines logic), even if distant. Do NOT change the name-matching call (the one whose system text starts 'You match names in a story game'): it keeps its full list so references to distant things still resolve.
5. WHERE line: when the protagonist is not together with the scene location, or is sitting in a seat, add ONE first bullet to the SCENE section built only from tree names, in this form: '<protagonist name> is in the <seat name> of <vehicle name>, <area name>.' when seated, or '<protagonist name> is <area name>.' otherwise (for example 'Kristin is in the driver's seat of Kristin's truck, outside the house.'). When the protagonist is together with the scene location and not seated, add NOTHING.
6. BYTE IDENTITY: for every state in which the protagonist is together with the scene location and not seated, the narrator prompt (system and user) must be byte-identical to today's. Prove it: BEFORE any code change, generate golden prompts with the stubbed network (use .plans/world-model-s1/prompt_capture.py's technique: patch storygame.runtime.cloudflare.urlopen, build the product-wired provider with storygame.runtime.capture.build_capture_provider and a stub Jev) for Scene 1A with Kristin in mcgehee_home and in the kitchen, for the command 'Look around.', and for the entry states of scenes 1B and 2A (bootstrap helpers exist in tests/test_1b_spine_prompts.py, tests/test_2a_spine_prompts.py); save them under tests/fixtures/place_feed/ and assert equality after the change.

TESTS FIRST. Write tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py and the golden fixtures BEFORE the code, see the new behavior tests fail, then implement. Cases: (a) goldens equal (item 6); (b) 1A, Kristin at outside_house, 'Look around.': the narration user prompt contains the outside description, the truck, the laptop and the house gate, and contains none of: drawer, pens, stapler, spare batteries, Michelle's phone, workstation, workstation chair, 'back door has been forced', 'thin gap'; (c) 1A, Kristin in truck_driver_seat: same, plus the WHERE bullet exactly 'Kristin is in the driver's seat of Kristin's truck, outside the house.' and 'Kristin. Place: driver's seat.' still present; (d) 'Open the drawer.' while outside keeps the drawer listed (command-referred); (e) the name-matching call prompt for 'Look around.' outside still lists the house things; (f) with the card recovered and the pointer statements committed, they appear in the prompt inside the house and not outside; (g) a SYNTHETIC second story (reuse tests/test_cue_eligibility_compare.py `_synthetic_package()` or build the smallest package with two areas, a scene location, a described second area, a seat and a reach-annotated statement) proving 2 to 5 with no Kristin-specific logic. Keep the file small and complete.

FINISH: ruff format and ruff check every .py you touched; run the focused suites in the check until they pass; report every existing test you changed and why, and show the (b) and (c) prompts' SCENE and THINGS sections in your final message.
